sections.h2: Diesel barely tracks retail inflation: r = +0.11 against headline CPI

chart.title: Only the wholesale link is strong; diesel against retail CPI is near zero
chart.sub: Pearson r of year-on-year growth, April anchor, FY2012–FY2026.
chart.source: DPIIT Office of the Economic Adviser (WPI, 2011-12 = 100); MoSPI (CPI); author's calculation.

sections.means: Diesel tracks the wholesale index almost perfectly but shows no measurable link to headline retail inflation at annual frequency.
sections.todo: Test pass-through at monthly frequency and control for crude before treating the freight-to-inflation story as settled.

sections.h2: Private diesel sales fell 34.7% in May 2026 while public-sector sales rose 6.9%

chart.title: Private marketers' May diesel sales fell 34.7% on the year before
chart.sub: Diesel sales growth, May 2026 against May 2025, %.
chart.source: PPAC, Industry Consumption Report POL & NG, May 2026.

sections.means: The ₹40 gap between direct-sales and retail diesel draws bulk buyers to the pump and cuts private marketers' volume sharply.
sections.todo: Close the tax wedge on commercial fleet fuel while converting those fleets to gas, rather than cutting the retail diesel price.

sections.h2: Every freight indicator grew faster than diesel demand's 1.6% in May 2026

chart.title: Freight activity grew several times faster than diesel burn
chart.source: PPAC Industry Consumption Report, May 2026, drawing on GSTN, FADA and ipa.nic.in.

sections.means: Freight proxies ran well ahead of diesel consumption, a gap the post leaves as an open question rather than explaining away.
sections.todo: Establish what else is carrying freight before attributing the gap to rail or efficiency.

sections.h2: CNG costs 26% less per km than diesel in a sedan and 25% less in an SUV

sections.means: On the modelled four-wheeler basis CNG is cheaper per kilometre than diesel, but the figures are for passenger cars only.
